title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 122
paragraphs: This Callias deserves to be remembered by everyone for a number of reasons: first, as already said, because he was an excellent man in the cause of his country's freedom; then for what he did at the Olympic games, where he won the horse race and came in second in the chariot race, having already before won at the Pythian games, so that he was distinguished in the eyes of all Greece by the sums he spent; and finally because he showed himself so generous with his three daughters, for when they came of age for marriage he gave each of them a most splendid dowry and also indulged their wishes — whichever man in Athens each one chose as her husband, to that man he gave her.
